requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the requirement is implemented and tested. I found one minor edge case, described at the end, that I did not count as a gap.

**Mandatory (initial) set**
- `AssessmentSources::prepare` (src/authoring/inputs.rs 42-173) builds the subject, cited-requirement, `{impl}`/`{test}` and anchor selectors.
- It then calls `definition_inputs` (inputs.rs 416-441) over those contributed inputs, passing the subject text as well. Any term referenced by the subject or by a contributed source is therefore picked up.
- `definition_inputs` calls `terms::dependencies` and turns each result into an `InputSelector::Definition` through `source_input`.
- `InputSelector::resolve` for a definition returns `raw_lines`, the full fenced declaration including the `:phrase:` option. The tests assert that `text[0]` starts with `:::{definition}` and `text[1]` starts with `:phrase:`.
- Transitivity and cycle safety come from `terms::close_dependencies` (src/terms.rs 124-153). It works as a fixed point with a `visited` set, so there are no duplicates and cycles terminate.
- `prepare` also guards against duplicates by checking `!mandatory.contains(&input)`.

**Additional reads**
- `tools::read` and `tools::search` (src/authoring/tools.rs 80-123 and 337-480) compute `sources.additional_definitions(...)` for every delivered input. The result is returned to the model and appended to `ToolDelivery.inputs`.
- `additional_definitions` (inputs.rs 262-278) removes definitions that were already delivered or recorded.
- `assess` (src/authoring/mod.rs 416-545) collects delivered inputs in `pending`. It calls `sources.record_inputs(&pending)` right after the next provider response and before any submission is accepted. The definitions are therefore supplied first and recorded before acceptance.
- `record_inputs` deduplicates, and definition inputs are kept in full by `recorded_input`.

**Tests**
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (inputs.rs) uses two terms that reference each other, so it covers a cycle. It asserts exactly two definition inputs, which covers transitivity and no duplicates. It also checks that a term referenced only through the subject is included.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` checks that a term referenced from a contributed source's comment is included, and that an unstaged terms file is reported.
- `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` (mod.rs 630-686) covers the follow-up path:
  - a read introduces `terms.value`, which pulls in `terms.unit` transitively;
  - the recorded evidence contains each definition exactly once and in full, with the phrase option;
  - the definition text appears in the second request, which is the one that precedes the submission, and not in the first.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` (tools.rs) covers the `habeas` read path, including the definitions returned and the dedup on record.

**Marking and scope**
- All code implementing the requirement carries `{impl}` markers: `prepare`, `record_inputs`, `additional_definitions`, `source_input`, `definition_inputs`, `assess`, `read` and `search`.
- The dependency computation in `terms.rs` is marked with `requirements.definitions.dependencies` and `requirements.definitions.selection`, which are separate requirements that specify it.
- I saw no unspecified extra behavior.

**Minor edge case (not counted as a gap)**
- Within one turn, two tool calls that reach the same new term could each return that definition to the model. `additional_definitions` filters only against already-recorded inputs, not against inputs still pending. The recorded evidence is still deduplicated.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
